prompt:
Score each onboarding change. Sub-scores:
- impact 0-3: how many users the targeted step loses and how much this could recover
- evidence 0-3: whether the funnel and the support mail both point at this problem
- confidence 0-2: how likely this kind of change works, judged from the lessons below
- cost 0-2: 2 = config only, 0 = needs new screens and a release
Also give predicted_lift: expected relative change in the target step's conversion, e.g. 0.05.

Lessons from earlier weeks:
Reordering onboarding flows can produce major wins (up to +12.0%), but carries risk of severe drops (-8.9%) or no clear effect, with predictions often being inaccurate.
Targeted copy changes for account persistence (+3.5%) and launch call-to-actions (+6.7%) were helpful, with launch CTA performance underpredicted (+0.5% predicted vs +6.7% measured); general intro copy showed no clear effect.
Introducing new interactive flows was helpful (+7.2% measured vs +2.0% predicted), outperforming initial predictions.
UI redesigns yielded zero winning tests and carried severe downside risk (down to -19.3%), consistently performing worse than predicted or showing no clear effect.
Hints showed no wins, either actively hurting performance (-3.1%) or producing no clear effect.
Notifications, layout changes, and waiting screen progress indicators showed no clear effect across all tested rounds.

Measured so far, by kind of change (relative change on the target step):
- adoption, copy: +2.9% over 1 test(s)
- adoption, hint: +1.8% over 1 test(s)
- adoption, redesign: -12.5% over 3 test(s)
- choose_path, copy: +0.2% over 1 test(s)
- choose_path, hint: -3.1% over 1 test(s)
- choose_path, redesign: +0.4% over 1 test(s)
- choose_path, reorder: +3.1% over 1 test(s)
- finish, copy: +6.7% over 1 test(s)
- finish, layout: -4.4% over 2 test(s)
- finish, new_flow: +7.2% over 1 test(s)
- finish, redesign: -8.6% over 2 test(s)
- home, hint: -0.0% over 1 test(s)
- home, notification: -1.3% over 2 test(s)
- home, wait_info: +1.0% over 3 test(s)
- sign_in, copy: +3.5% over 1 test(s)
- sign_in, reorder: +1.2% over 6 test(s)

Funnel:
- choose_path: 78.3%, median 8s / mean 514s
- sign_in: 85.2%, median 3s / mean 567s
- adoption: 60.9%, median 89s / mean 1017s
- home: 81.3%, median 201s / mean 2336s
- finish: 73.5%, median 395s / mean 5815s

Changes:
0: [sign_in, reorder] Reorder Sign-In After Adoption Certificate: Move sign-in to take place immediately after the adoption certificate screen so users complete companion creation before being asked to create an account. (why: Adoption step has the biggest drop-off (60.9% conversion). Allowing users to finalize their pet certificate before signing in builds emotional ownership.)
1: [finish, new_screen] Interactive Audio Preview Screen: Introduce a new interactive sound test screen before home intro where users can sample desktop pet sound alerts and call cues. (why: Finish step has a very high mean time (5815s) and multiple support emails noted confusion about how to hear or interact with their pet.)
2: [finish, copy] Desktop Hotkey Controls Launch CTA: Update home intro button and body text to clearly explain the shortcut hotkey for summoning, hiding, and opening pet controls. (why: Launch CTA copy changes previously yielded +6.7%, and 3 support emails reported post-onboarding confusion regarding hiding and controlling the pet.)
3: [home, wait_info] Interactive Pet Animation Waiting Screen: Add an interactive pet animation preview and play trigger button to the waiting screen while background assets render. (why: The waiting step has a long mean duration (2336s). Interactive preview elements engage users while asset rendering finishes.)

scores.note: Targeting the biggest drop-off step (Adoption), but flow reordering carries variable confidence.
Interactive flows perform strongly (+7.2%) and address clear user complaints, though require new screen development.
Launch CTA copy updates previously yielded +6.7% and directly answer frequent support questions at config-only cost.
Wait screen updates historically show negligible impact (+1.0%) across multiple tests.
